verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's docs assert CUDA-X/RAPIDS compatibility and position the card as an 'AI powerhouse' for LLM fine-tuning, backed by the general CUDA toolkit docs, but there is no explicit PyTorch build/support-matrix citation for this SKU. A hands-on community report (comm-4) directly contradicts full mainstream-framework readiness, noting the card's SM120 architecture lacks tmem/tcgen05 support and that 'main libraries' have not caught up, unlike newer B300/SM100 parts. missing for 10: an official PyTorch/CUDA support-matrix entry naming RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell SM120), and resolution of the SM120 library-support gap noted by users.
